text:
maria: Heads up — starting ~09:12 UTC we're seeing a spike of mTLS handshake failures in ap-south and eu-west proxies. Spike lines up with yesterday's keystore RBAC tighten.
jordan: On it. any sample logs?
maria: ```
ap-proxy[ingress] 2024-04-05T09:12:23Z HANDSHAKE_ERR peer=svc-a tls: certificate verify failed: certificate signed by unknown authority\nverify: validate chain: missing intermediate\n``` 
devon: That looks like the rotator returned an incomplete chain. @maria can you run: ```kubectl exec -n infra keystore-rotator-0 -- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/keys/service-a``` ?
maria: ```{\n  "name": "service-a",\n  "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...",\n  "intermediate_chain": null,\n  "issued_at": "2024-03-10T12:00:00Z"\n}```
irene: Checking audit logs for KMS unwrap calls now — seeing DENY events for the rotator service account.
audit-bot: CloudKMS: 5 DENY events for key projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/unwrap between 09:11 and 09:14 UTC (caller=serviceAccount:keystore-rotator@prod)
kevin: Who merged the RBAC change? @devon or infra team?
devon: That was me — merged the role tighten PR last night (PR 4218). I removed roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter from keystore-rotator@prod to narrow blast radius.
maria: That explains it. Without decrypt/unwrap permission the rotator cannot unwrap the key material to build a full chain -> proxies get partial certs -> handshake fails.
jordan: Immediate mitigation: re-grant decrypt permission temporarily and restart keystore-rotator to unblock traffic. Also add fallback in rotator: if unwrap fails, serve the last known-good full chain from cache.
devon: Applying temp IAM binding: ```gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding prod --member=serviceAccount:keystore-rotator@prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter``` — pushing now.
maria: Grant applied, rotator restarted. ap-south handshakes recovered within ~90s. Monitoring shows handshake error rate returning to baseline.
irene: We need a post-incident checklist: 1) Why did CI/PR not catch this? 2) Why no KMS DENY alert fired? 3) Why rotator didn't fallback to cached chain gracefully?
kevin: For vuln triage: this change removed permission (so not a privilege escalation) but it created availability impact. We should ensure RBAC automation has guardrails for service accounts that perform crypto ops.
devon: Agreed. Proposing immediate actions: (a) add a CI preflight stage that runs `keystore-rotator --canary-unwrap` against a test key whenever KMS IAM changes are proposed; (b) add an alert for any CloudKMS DENY on prod rotator SAs; (c) add a rotator fallback path to serve cached full chain and emit a high-severity log when unwrap fails.
jordan: I'll open the incident ticket and assign owners: SecEng (irene) + SRE (maria) + Infra (devon). Also add a shortblameline for oncall to revert RBAC if availability degrades.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-0485 — Keystore unwrap failures causing mTLS handshakes. Severity: P1. Links: https://incident.triage/INC-2024-0485
maria: Long-term recommendations: - move sensitive key material in KMS with HSM + strict principals but ensure preflight.Canary exists; - include KMS unwrap smoke tests in rollouts; - add an audit log SLO that triggers PagerDuty for DENY on critical SAs.
kevin: Also review TLS config hardening: don't rely on client to supply intermediates if we can serve full chain. Add a rule in the rotator to validate chain completeness before publishing to proxies.
irene: For the postmortem I'll capture timeline, PR diff, audit-log evidence (KMS DENY events), and remediation steps. Will also include a small runbook patch: if keystore-rotator unwrap fails -> reapply short-lived decrypt role + restart -> rotate affected certs once stable.
devon: I'll patch the RBAC terraform module to require a smoke-test target when removing any `cloudkms.*` role from service accounts tagged with `role=keystore-rotator`.
maria: Thanks everyone. Good catch — saved the region failover. :thumbsup:
kevin: Posting followup doc in #eng-security-postmortems after we wrap up. Please add any extra logs or timing details here.
maria: Adding the proxy debug snippet used earlier: ```sudo journalctl -u ap-proxy -n 200 | grep -i handshake | tail -n 50``` 
jordan: Closing loop: rotator fallback patch + CI test + KMS DENY alert — owners assigned. We'll schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow 14:00 UTC.
